neighbours.label: a spatial preposition whose object is a global geographic place (continent, ocean, pole, equator, the world)
fire: Penguins live in the cold seas south of Antarctica and nowhere else.
The warm currents flow along the eastern coast of Australia.
These turtles nest on beaches close to the equator every spring.
Magellan's crew was the first to sail around the globe.
Ants are found on every continent except Antarctica.
The research ship drifted for months in the ice near the North Pole.
Monsoon winds sweep across the Indian Ocean each summer.
The western shore of South America faces the open Pacific.
quiet: Penguins live in the cold pool south of the zoo entrance.
The warm water flows along the eastern wall of the bathtub.
These turtles nest in a tank close to the window every spring.
Our crew was the first to sail around the small lake.
Ants are found in every room except the kitchen.
The toy boat drifted for hours in the pond near the playground.
Cool winds sweep across the parking lot each evening.
The western side of the house faces the open garden.

notes: card: top peaks on ' of', ' near', ' to', ' around', ' except' right before Africa, the equator, the ice pack, the world, Antarctica, the South Pole. Near misses keep the prepositions with local, non-global objects.
